claim: Krebs 1931-32 urea cycle: step order is known from Holmes's reconstruction as paraphrased by Kulkarni and Simon (opened): 26 Jul to 15 Nov 1931 screen and known work, ornithine surprise on 15 Nov (about 3.5 months in); 15 Nov to mid Jan scope check, none of the derivatives worked; 14 Jan new apparatus, ammonia as nitrogen source by 23 Jan; catalyst idea, arginase link, 13 Apr test of 24.5 urea per ornithine, citrulline 25 Apr. Holmes 1980 and Grasshoff and May 2003 text were not opened; no count of experiments is verified.
agent_test: Take one fully logged agent run, hide the order, have a second model rebuild the operator order from the notes, and score match to the true trace.

claim: Reconstruction of a scientist step order has rival readings (historian tidy story, later recall, true contemporaneous record). No inter-rater statistic exists in the sources opened.
agent_test: Have two independent reconstructors rebuild order from the same agent log; report rank agreement between them.

claim: KEKADA (opened, Kulkarni and Simon 1988) encodes surprise-driven focusing: if an outcome violates its expectation, note a surprise and make it the focus; then study a subprocess or the scope across a class; failed effort is counted per hypothesis. The paper itself warns the early alanine surprise was probably not felt by Krebs, so surprise can make the record look tidier than it was.
agent_test: Compare an arm with a forced explain-the-surprise step before the next action against baseline at equal tokens on hidden-structure tasks.

claim: Frontier LLM agents fail most full discovery tasks. DiscoveryWorld: best agent completes 38% of easy and 18% of challenge tasks, 11 human scientists average 66% completion and 55% knowledge. DiscoveryBench: best about 25%. ScienceAgentBench: best 32.4% (34.3% with expert knowledge), o1-preview 42.2%. FIRE-Bench: best F1 46.7 (SD 23.4). All re-opened and confirmed.
agent_test: Run a baseline arm on a held-out slice of one benchmark; it is the reference for every scaffold comparison.

claim: Human scientists also brute-force instead of explaining: DiscoveryWorld human knowledge score (55%) is below completion (66%).
agent_test: Score completion and explanatory knowledge separately so brute force is not counted as discovery.

claim: Agent knowledge discovery falls with difficulty: ReAct knowledge 0.25 (easy) to 0.10 (challenge); Hypothesizer 0.34 to 0.08 (columns are procedure/completion/knowledge). ReAct completion also falls 0.38 to 0.18, so the claim in b13 that completion barely falls is wrong.
agent_test: Report difficulty-split knowledge score for our agent.

claim: A plain execution-feedback self-debug loop beats a heavy agent framework at far lower cost: Claude-3.5-Sonnet 32.4% vs OpenHands CodeAct 21.6%, $0.057 vs $0.958 per task; direct prompting 16.7%.
agent_test: Equal-token test: self-debug loop vs multi-step planner on code-execution tasks.

claim: Self-correction without an external signal does not help and often hurts: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 (round 1), GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0. With oracle labels GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3, but that is a leak, not a method. Update: for reasoning models the picture is different. Tsui 2026 finds a small or negative self-correction blind spot in reasoning models, and a Wait cue lifts non-reasoning models close to them (DeepSeek-V3 0.567 to 0.902 vs R1-0528 0.908). No exact Huang-protocol replication on o-series or R1 was found.
schema_part: G, S9 (look back needs external evidence)
agent_test: Run S9 look-back with and without a real check (test, execution) at equal tokens; expect gain only with the check.

claim: Persistent notes help only if they feed decisions. Hypothesizer keeps a status-tagged hypothesis notebook (cap 40 entries, 2k tokens, summary every 10 actions) yet scores low; AI Scientist keeps notes.txt. No ablation of the notebook alone was found.
agent_test: Ablate the structured notebook (hypothesis before, outcome after) at equal tokens.

claim: LLM-written research results are often wrong or invented. AI Scientist: invented ablation tables, unfair comparison after a metric change. Independent re-run: 5 of 12 experiments (42%) failed from coding errors, 4 of 7 manuscripts (57%) had structural errors and 4 of 7 (57%) had incorrect or hallucinated numbers.
agent_test: Check that every number in the final answer appears in a logged observation; count violations.

claim: Model judges overrate: Agent Laboratory automated score 6.1/10 vs human 3.8/10; best LLM judge 53.3% balanced accuracy vs 56.1% human inter-reviewer agreement.
agent_test: Compare self-grade vs external grade of our agent outputs.

claim: Idea generation collapses to repeats at scale: of 4000 seed ideas per topic only about 200 were non-duplicate, yet AI ideas rated more novel (5.64 vs 4.84, N=49 per condition, 79 reviewers, p<0.05) and slightly less feasible.
agent_test: Measure unique-hypothesis rate over N samples with and without a diversify operator.

claim: Acting on the system beats watching it: GPT-4o with its own interventions beats observation-only and beats replay of its own intervention data (yoked). Gains by complexity -0.6 to +12.7. Analyze-then-query: program 50.8 vs plain 43.4.
agent_test: Equal-query test: agent-chosen queries vs random or replayed queries.

claim: Two model-building failure modes: overcomplication (program: 17 of 20 failures) and overlooking (math equation: 16 of 20). Sample is 20 failures per box from the observation-only condition.
agent_test: Tag impasses in our traces as overcomplication or overlooking; test a simplicity operator vs a use-all-data operator.

claim: Code tools push strong models toward exploitation: exploration tokens (What if, Alternatively) fall and confirm/verify tokens rise with code budget; performance drops for strong models, weak models gain. Noise of 0.0001 cuts symbolic accuracy 12-16%.
agent_test: Track exploration-token rate vs tool budget in our agent.

claim: Long loops anchor greedily. In one 100-experiment case, one early hypothesis gave +21.41 of +26.92 points (79.5%), acceptance fell from 36-38% to 12%, and the agent wrote pivot then made another small nearby change. Literature access raised code-changing hypotheses 5% (2/42) to 76% (16/21). Controlled tests: AutoDiscovery at 500 evaluations finds greedy search loses efficiency over time with GPT-4o but equals MCTS with o4-mini; in MLE-bench, changing greedy to MCTS or the exploration constant gave only marginal change with AIDE operators.
agent_test: Impasse rule banning the same operator family after N rejections; compare gain at equal tokens.

claim: Failures concentrate in planning and conclusions: FIRE-Bench false positives 76.4% to 95.0% contradictory or unrelated; backbone upgrade gave +6.1 F1 for +21% cost.
agent_test: Apply a conclusion-vs-evidence audit at S9; count unsupported claims.

claim: State tracking breaks before reasoning: Auto-Discovery-Bench 10-house relational graph, Grok-4 and Gemini-2.5-pro 100%, GPT-4o 30%, Qwen2.5 0%; failures persist when intervention choice and hypothesis writing are supplied.
agent_test: Give an explicit state table and test.

claim: More attempts help: MLE-bench o1-preview bronze 16.9% at one try, 34.1% at pass@8.
agent_test: Equal-token compare of best-of-N vs one long chain.

claim: No 2020-2026 LLM study located replays a historical notebook (Krebs, Darwin, Faraday) and scores operator order against the record. Only a blog (Panchekha, Kepler-style synthetic data, n=1, ChatGPT Pro 67 min, no ellipse) was read. Search tools were throttled, so absence is not proven.
agent_test: Gap: a study is possible but untested.

claim: KEKADA is a partial reproduction with no reported match rate. It rediscovered the cycle in three scenarios (catalysis late, early but low, early and high), several key steps were chosen by the user (about 10 asterisk steps counted), and scenario 3 is judged unlikely against history. No independent replication found.
agent_test: Do not cite a match percentage for KEKADA. Score our agent's order against its own log instead.

claim: Krebs's anomaly was a single large miss inside a long routine stretch: about 4 weeks on known ammonia work and 3.5 months before ornithine plus ammonia gave urea at about double the expected rate. A surprise rule should fire on size of miss, not on every deviation.
agent_test: Trigger the explain-first rule only when the miss exceeds a stated band around the expected value.

claim: Surprise as a search signal helps at fixed budget: AutoDiscovery (Bayesian surprise as reward, 500 evaluations, same GPT-4o agent) finds 5-29% more surprising discoveries than strong search baselines, best on 17 of 21 datasets; 67% of its surprises were also surprising to experts. This tests surprise-directed search, not explain-before-moving-on, and budget is evaluations, not tokens.
agent_test: Add an equal-token arm that forces a written explanation of the largest miss before the next experiment.

claim: Written explanation after a failed test is what carries the gain in Reflexion: HumanEval Rust hardest 50, GPT-4, base 0.60, no reflection 0.60, no test generation 0.52, full 0.68; HotPotQA reflection adds 8 points over episodic memory alone. Needs an external test result; not equal tokens.
agent_test: Hypothesis-before, outcome-after note: ablate the explanation line at equal tokens.

claim: A memory of past attempts alone did not help in MLE-bench: AIDE with and without memory had nearly identical medal rates. Better operators did (45.5% vs 39.8%), as did scoped memory plus complexity cues bundled together, so the notebook-alone effect is unmeasured.
agent_test: Test an operator-level rule (show sibling failures, raise change size) rather than a global log.

claim: Search policy matters less than operators: with AIDE operators, greedy, MCTS and evolutionary search, and exploration constants 0 to 0.75, gave only marginal differences; validation score kept rising while held-out test plateaued or fell (overfitting to the checker).
agent_test: Impasse bans should change the operator, not only the node chosen. Judge on a held-out check.

claim: Darwin timeline from a secondary summary only: notebook B opened mid-July 1837 (tree sketch on page 36); Malthus insight noted 28 September 1838, about 14 months later; M notebook about 60 pages on man and morals. Gruber's counts of entries per topic and the critical readings (Kohn, Schweber, Ospovat) were not obtained.
agent_test: Treat Darwin as parallel streams plus an outside trigger; no counts are available to test.

claim: No measured agreement between independent reconstructions of one notebook was found. Dunbar's rate of unexpected findings was also not verified. Both remain open.
agent_test: Have two models rebuild the order from the same agent log and score agreement.
